notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1787). Words follow the Schirmer vocal score's spelling and punctuation, and its repeats of words and lines. Where the print differs from the libretto the words follow the print: Masetto "pormi vo'" (libretto por mi vo'), Zerlina "quell' ingrato" and "Ah! sei vede il sposo mio" (libretto s'ei; sung s'ei, if he), "sò", Giovanni "Sù!", "ed a tutti a abbondanza" (libretto in abbondanza), "gran rifreschi" (libretto rinfreschi), "non scoppar" (libretto scappar), "gioja", "E chiuso là" and "dì,", Masetto and Zerlina "andiamo tutti tre" (libretto tutti e tre), Leporello "Zi! zi!" and Anna "Io temo pel caro sposo". The servants' chorus ("Sù, svegliatevi da bravi") is played but has no part to practise. The piece ends on the last bar before the Adagio: Leporello's "d'amor" is cut there, its first syllable "d'a-" sung in this piece and "-mor!" on the first bar of the next ("Protegga il giusto cielo"). IPA, word meanings and translations were drafted for this app (S28) and the IPA was checked against Castel. IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ. Translation literal, for meaning.
